channel.title: KCBS | CBS LA - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from KCBS | CBS LA (cbsla.com)

item.title: Hegseth says U.S. torpedo sank an Iranian warship as military campaign ramps up
item.description: In Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's second news briefing since the start of the Iran war, Hegseth said the U.S. had sunk an enemy ship by a torpedo for the first time since World War II.

item.title: Rep. Tony Gonzales admits to affair with former staffer, calling it a "mistake"
item.description: Republican Rep. Tony Gonzales of Texas acknowledged for the first time Wednesday that he had a relationship with a former staffer, but alleged the controversy that has engulfed the situation is "about power and money."

item.title: 3/4: CBS Evening News
item.description: U.S. submarine sinks Iranian warship as Tehran widens ring of retaliation; CBS News producer George Osterkamp dies at 82

item.title: Lou Holtz, former Notre Dame football coach, dies at age 89
item.description: Holtz coached Notre Dame from 1986 to 1996, winning 100 games with the school, including a 12-0 national title-winning season in 1988.

item.title: Sister of U.S. service member killed in Iran: "I still don't fully think it's real"
item.description: Five of the six American service members who were killed in the Iran war have been positively identified. The father and sister of 20-year-old Sgt. Declan J. Coady, one of the deceased, remembers him.

item.title: Pentagon releases names of U.S. service members killed in Iran war
item.description: Six American service members have been killed in the U.S.-Iran conflict, U.S. Central Command said.

item.title: What we know about U.S. service members killed in Iran war
item.description: The fallen soldiers identified by the Pentagon were Sgt. Declan Coady, Sgt. 1st Class Nicole Amor, Capt. Cody Khork, Sgt. 1st Class Noah Tietjens, Maj. Jeffrey R. O'Brien and Chief Warrant Officer 3 Robert M. Marzan.

item.title: 3/4: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: White House defends evacuations of Americans in the Middle East despite major delays; Vice President Vance defends Iran War despite years of calling for anti-interventionism

item.title: GOP senator joins police in ejecting protester from Capitol Hill hearing
item.description: A Senate Republican assisted several police officers in ejecting a man who interrupted a Capitol Hill hearing on Wednesday to object to the U.S. and Israel's war with Iran.

item.title: Hegseth says U.S. "just getting started" as Iran war spreads
item.description: The U.S. is "accelerating, not decelerating" war on Iran, Hegseth says, as strikes intensify in the region and reach 1,000 miles away.
